Below is a **complete, minimal‑but‑functional** Rust project that

1. Reads the current clipboard text (Windows, macOS, Linux).
2. Sends that text to ElevenLabs’ Text‑to‑Speech API.
3. Streams the returned MP3/OGG audio directly to your speakers.

> **⚠️  Disclaimer** – ElevenLabs’ API is paid.  
>  You’ll need a valid API key and a voice ID.  
>  The example uses the “eleven_monolingual_v1” voice (the free one).  
>  Replace it with your own voice ID if you want a different voice.

---

## 1. Project layout

```
elevenlabs-tts/
├─ Cargo.toml
└─ src/
   └─ main.rs
```

---

## 2. Cargo.toml

```toml
[package]
name = "elevenlabs-tts"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

# Optional: enable the `clipboard-win` feature on Windows
# (the default `clipboard` crate auto‑detects the platform)
[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }          # async runtime
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }  # HTTP client
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }        # JSON (de)serialization
serde_json = "1"
clipboard = "0.5"                                       # cross‑platform clipboard
rodio = "0.17"                                          # audio playback
bytes = "1"                                             # for reading the stream
dotenvy = "0.15"                                        # load .env (optional)
```

> **Why these crates?**  
> * `tokio` – async runtime needed by `reqwest`.  
> * `reqwest` – HTTP client that supports streaming.  
> * `serde`/`serde_json` – parse JSON responses.  
> * `clipboard` – read the system clipboard.  
> * `rodio` – play audio from a byte buffer.  
> * `bytes` – convenient stream reader.  
> * `dotenvy` – optional, lets you keep your API key in a `.env` file.

**1. How do I create a new document in Microsoft Word?**  
    To create a new document, open Word and click the **File** tab, then select **New**. You can choose a blank document or a template from the available options. Alternatively, press **Ctrl + N** on the keyboard to open a new blank document instantly.

**2. What is the difference between “Save” and “Save As” in Word?**  
    **Save** updates the current file with any changes you’ve made. **Save As** creates a new copy of the document, allowing you to specify a different file name, location, or format (e.g., .docx, .pdf, .txt). Use **Save As** when you want to preserve the original file or change its format.

**3. How can I insert a table into a Word document?**  
    Place the cursor where you want the table. Go to the **Insert** tab, click **Table**, then drag to select the number of rows and columns or click **Insert Table…** to specify exact dimensions. Word will insert the table at the cursor position.

**4. What are the steps to apply a heading style to a paragraph?**  
    Select the paragraph, then go to the **Home** tab. In the **Styles** group, click the desired heading style (e.g., **Heading 1**, **Heading 2**). This applies consistent formatting and enables automatic table of contents generation.

**5. How do I add page numbers to a Word document?**  
    Click the **Insert** tab, then **Page Number**. Choose the position (top, bottom, or margin) and alignment. Word will insert page numbers automatically on every page. You can format them further by selecting **Format Page Numbers…**.

**6. What is the purpose of the “Track Changes” feature?**  
    **Track Changes** records all edits (insertions, deletions, formatting changes) made to a document. Each change is highlighted and annotated, allowing reviewers to accept or reject modifications. Activate it via **Review → Track Changes**.

**7. How can I insert a hyperlink that opens a web page?**  
    Select the text or object you want to link, then press **Ctrl + K** or go to **Insert → Hyperlink**. In the dialog, type or paste the URL in the **Address** field, then click **OK**. The selected text becomes a clickable link.

**8. How do I change the default font and size for new documents?**  
    Open **File → Options → General**. Under **When creating new documents**, click **Set Default Font…**. Choose your preferred font and size, then click **OK**. All future documents will use these defaults unless overridden.
